provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Auto family batch, quote archetype. Insurance-referral driven, so copy explains the claim process without giving legal or insurance advice and never names an insurer, estimating system or paint maker. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What happens after the accident: filing the claim, the adjuster's estimate, supplements when hidden damage turns up, the deductible, and questions to ask your insurer about choosing a collision shop
pageStructurePlus.why: Drivers after a wreck are confused and anxious, and most assume the insurer picks the shop. A calm walkthrough is what gets the car towed to this body shop.

pageStructurePlus.section: Paintless dent repair and hail damage
pageStructurePlus.contains: When PDR works and when a panel needs filler and paint, door dings, crease dents, hail storms, and what a hail repair day looks like
pageStructurePlus.why: PDR and hail work are separate searches with their own urgency. After a storm, the body shop that explains PDR clearly gets the line of dented cars.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Reading the factory color code, blending into adjacent panels, tri-coat and pearl finishes, clear coat, and why a bumper can look different under a parking-lot light
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners worry the repaired panel won't match. Explaining color matching is how a collision shop shows craft beyond the insurer's estimate.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Frame measuring, structural pulls, pre- and post-repair scans, and recalibrating the cameras and radar behind a bumper or windshield after collision repair
pageStructurePlus.why: Modern cars hide sensors in the panels. Owners and adjusters trust a body shop that names the calibration step instead of skipping it.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Getting the wrecked car moved from the tow yard, avoiding daily storage fees, rental car coordination, and how long a typical repair keeps the car in the shop
pageStructurePlus.why: The days after a collision are logistics. The body shop that handles the tow yard and the rental removes the reason to go elsewhere.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What each parts type means on the estimate, fit and finish differences, when the shop recommends factory parts, and how to ask about it
pageStructurePlus.why: Parts type is the one line on the estimate owners notice. A plain explanation makes the shop look honest rather than defensive.

designDirections.name: Claim Desk
designDirections.bestFor: Single-location body shops that need the estimate request and claim help in front of a stressed driver
designDirections.headlineSample: Collision repair in {City}, we handle the claim
designDirections.whyItFits: Clean white and cobalt read like a well-run front office. The neutral sans keeps the claim steps and estimate button readable for someone shaken after a wreck.

designDirections.name: Straight Panels
designDirections.bestFor: Body shops with strong before-and-after work, paint matching and PDR to show
designDirections.headlineSample: Auto body and paint, done right in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo. A near-black ground shows crumpled metal and the finished gloss the way a shop light does, and the before-after hero is the whole sales pitch.

designDirections.name: Repair Record
designDirections.bestFor: Established collision centers with calibration equipment, fleet accounts and long insurer relationships
designDirections.headlineSample: Collision repair and sensor calibration for {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Evergreen and a classical serif read like insurance-grade trust, which is what owners of newer, sensor-heavy cars want before they hand over the keys.

openers.line: Your body shop's listing has strong reviews but no website. A driver who just had a fender-bender in {City} wants to see your collision work before deciding where to tow the car.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what could sit behind that button for the body shop: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website on your listing is a Facebook page. Fine for regulars, but someone with a crumpled bumper and a claim number wants to know how you handle insurance, not scroll a feed.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the latest repair they posted.
openers.linkLine: A body shop page that explains the claim: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your collision site still lists an old fax number and a stock photo of a car that isn't yours. Drivers choosing a body shop after an accident look for signs the place is current and careful.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for stock photos, an old copyright year or dead links. Note which.
openers.linkLine: Your body shop, current and careful: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone, your site's estimate button sits under three paragraphs. People request a collision estimate from the roadside or the tow yard, phone in hand.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone and note where the estimate button sits. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: An estimate request built for the roadside: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to send your shop pictures of the damage and get a rough estimate. After a minor collision, most drivers want a ballpark before they decide whether to file a claim at all.
openers.hook: Check the listing and any site for a damage-upload form. If there's none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A damage photo estimate form for the body shop: {demo-link}

openers.line: The quarter-panel rebuild and the color-matched door on your page are the best collision work I've seen locally. They're mixed in with lunch posts and nobody comparing body shops will find them.
openers.hook: Find two before-and-after repairs you can name by panel and vehicle. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your collision before-and-afters, sorted by repair: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention a body shop that dealt with the insurer for them and a paint match nobody can spot. That's exactly what a nervous driver needs to read, and it stays on your listing.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one line about the insurer, paint or communication. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the collision work they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: After the next hailstorm or the first icy week in {City}, every body shop's phone lights up at once. The ones with a dent and hail page catch the calls they can't answer.
openers.hook: Use right after a local hailstorm or ahead of winter. Name the storm or the month in the reply.
openers.linkLine: A hail and PDR page ready for the next storm: {demo-link}

openers.line: Most fender-benders happen on the commute home or on a weekend, when your shop is closed. A collision request form catches the driver before the tow yard sends them somewhere else.
openers.hook: Call after hours. If it rings out or hits a full voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A collision request that works on a Saturday night: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Hiring a body tech or painter
openers.line: Saw you're hiring a body tech or painter. Skilled refinish people look at a collision shop's work online before they apply, the same way a careful car owner does.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or job ad. Note the role and date.
openers.linkLine: A body shop page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: You repair cars from all over {City}, but nothing tells someone whose car got hit in {Neighborhood} that your body shop is the one to tow it to. That's the search they make from the tow truck.
openers.hook: Find towns named in their reviews. Use the furthest one.
openers.linkLine: A collision page for each town you pull from: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you help with deductibles or offer payments on out-of-pocket body work, put it on the page. A deductible is the number that makes people put off the repair.
openers.hook: Only if they mention payment help somewhere. Never imply a deductible offer they don't publish; if nothing is posted, skip this angle.
openers.linkLine: Payment options for collision work, explained: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your sign and listing mention factory training and a lifetime repair warranty. Showing those on a body shop page is what makes a driver of a newer car comfortable towing it to you.
openers.hook: Check sign, listing and posts for certifications or warranty terms. Note only what they publish; never add a credential.
openers.linkLine: Certifications and repair warranty on one collision page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like much of your collision work comes through insurer referrals. That can change with one contract, and owners who get to choose a body shop search for one themselves.
openers.hook: Look for mentions of insurance partners or 'direct repair' in reviews or signage. Never name the insurer back to them.
openers.linkLine: Where a driver choosing their own body shop would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is serious collision work. A repair like that should be the first thing someone sees when they're deciding where to take a wrecked car.
openers.hook: Pick the newest before-and-after and name it exactly: vehicle, panel and what was done.
openers.linkLine: That collision repair, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hey {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is serious collision work.

I looked for body shops in {City} and found {Business Name} on Maps and social, but no site that explains the insurance claim or takes damage pictures for an estimate. I put together a sample body shop page, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my last message got buried. Here's the sample body shop site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a claim walkthrough for drivers, a damage-upload estimate form, a PDR and hail page, and before-and-after collision work sorted by repair. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave you be.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for collision and body shops here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with an insurance claim walkthrough, a damage-upload estimate form and a before-and-after gallery, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many repair and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a shop your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, which is less than a single bumper-and-quarter-panel job."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and an invoice for the deposit. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: Insurance sends us most of our work.
objections.handler: "And that's worth protecting. The site is for the drivers who get to choose, and for the day a referral program changes. It also makes the shop look right when an adjuster checks you out."

objections.objection: We don't do estimates from pictures.
objections.handler: "Then the form just books the in-person estimate, with the damage pictures attached so you know if it's a scuff or a structural job before they arrive."

objections.objection: Our estimating system already has a customer portal.
objections.handler: "Good, I'll link it for repair status. The portal works once they've chosen you; the site is what gets them to choose you from the tow truck."

objections.objection: Every collision job is different, I can't post prices.
objections.handler: "You don't have to. The page explains how estimates and supplements work, and what drives cost. Honesty about the process sells better than a price."
"Then let the site sort the work: PDR and small dents to a photo form, big hits to a call. You spend counter time on the jobs that pay."
"{Build Range}. For your shop about {Build Price}: claim walkthrough, photo estimate form, gallery and a hail page. That's less than one panel job."

email.subject: Body shop site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for body shops in {City}, and put together a sample for {Business Name} with a claim walkthrough and a photo estimate form. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} body shop demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hey {Owner} — icy roads and hail season both bring a wave of collision calls, and the shops with a clear claim page catch the drivers who get to choose. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a fraction of one mid-size collision repair, never to an hourly rate.
The claim walkthrough is the page that wins self-pay and choose-your-shop drivers. Price it as its own line.
A photo estimate form that sorts PDR from structural damage is worth more than a contact form.
Only quote hail and PDR pages for shops that do PDR in-house or have a PDR partner they'll name.
Calibration pages are a line of their own, and only for shops with the equipment or a sublet partner.
Never write insurer names, referral program names or repair outcomes on any page; keep it to process.

lineItems.description: Max with a step-by-step timeline, a supplement explainer, a printable 'after an accident' checklist and an FAQ.
Max with guided angles for the upload, a claim-number field, a drivable yes-or-no and routing to the estimator.
Max with a storm banner they can switch on, a hail-day booking form and PDR before-and-afters.
Max when it explains pre- and post-scans, frame measuring and sensor recalibration with the shop's own process.
Max when the gallery filters by bumper, quarter panel, frame, paint and PDR with a slider for each pair.
Max when each page lists the tow route, nearby tow yards and reviews from that town.
Max when the claim walkthrough, estimate form and FAQ are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Teardown-to-delivery photo series
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "We follow one wrecked car through teardown, frame, paint booth and delivery. It becomes the gallery, a month of posts and proof of how the body shop works."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on a structural job the owner is proud of.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile management for collision work
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Weekly before-and-after posts with the panel and the town on the body shop's Google profile, plus answers to the claim questions people ask there."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests at vehicle delivery
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When the repaired car is picked up, the owner gets a text asking how the paint match and the claim went, with a review link."

whatElseYouSell.name: Post-storm hail response campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Within a day of a hailstorm, the hail page goes live, posts go out and past customers get a dent check invite from the body shop."
whatElseYouSell.when: Set up before hail season; run within a day of a storm.

whatElseYouSell.name: Tow driver referral cards
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A card tow drivers hand to shaken drivers at the scene: what to do next, and the collision shop that will handle it."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, after the claim walkthrough is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Fleet damage program sales sheet
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page sheet for local fleets: how the body shop handles van and truck damage, turnaround, and invoicing by unit."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, when they want more fleet work.

whatElseYouSell.name: Insurance agent leave-behind kit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Local independent insurance agents get a folder with the shop's claim walkthrough and repair warranty to hand clients who ask where to go."

withoutAI.route: Tow operators who bring wrecks to the shop
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The tow operator who drops wrecks at your body shop needs a site with a dispatch number and an accident page. I'll build it and your shop stays their first drop."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Tow-to-body-shop is the oldest referral in the trade. The owner's intro opens it.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The independent agent who sends clients your way runs a dated site. A claims-help page with a 'trusted repair shops' list is their real need."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents buy websites, and their clients ask where to fix the car. The shop sits on the list.

withoutAI.route: PDR technicians who work the shop's hail jobs
withoutAI.whoPays: The PDR tech, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The paintless dent tech you call after a hailstorm travels storm to storm with no site. Their bookings would come through yours."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: PDR techs depend on body shop partners. The referral is built in.

withoutAI.whoPays: The glass shop, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The glass and calibration shop you sublet to after front-end hits has the same thin site you had."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Collision jobs sublet glass and calibration every week. One introduction covers both.

withoutAI.route: Car rental branches near the shop
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The local rental agency that puts your customers in cars during repairs needs a site that takes replacement-rental bookings directly."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Independent rental agencies live on body shop referrals and buy sites to compete.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your paint and body supply rep sells to every collision shop in the region. Their site needs online ordering and a shop locator."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply houses have budget and a shop list that is your prospect list.

withAI.route: Accident-scene intake assistant for the tow company
withAI.pitchLine: "Drivers text the tow company from the scene; an assistant collects location, vehicle and whether it's drivable, and asks which body shop they want."
withAI.whyItWorks: Tow dispatch is overloaded after crashes. The collision shop becomes the default suggestion.

withAI.route: Claims question helper for insurance agencies
withAI.pitchLine: "Clients ask the agency 'what do I do after a fender-bender' at night. An assistant answers from the agency's own guide and lists their recommended shops."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents get the same claim questions daily. The body shop is on the answer list.

withAI.route: Hail-day booking assistant for the PDR tech
withAI.pitchLine: "After a storm, an assistant answers 'can you fix hail dents' and books dent assessment slots at the body shop for the PDR tech."
withAI.whyItWorks: Storm work is a scheduling rush. The body shop hosts the slots, so both sides win.

withAI.route: Calibration scheduling helper for the glass shop
withAI.pitchLine: "Body shops and drivers ask which cars need calibration after a windshield or bumper. An assistant answers from the glass shop's list and books the slot."
withAI.whyItWorks: Calibration is confusing and growing. The collision shop sends the first users.

withAI.route: Rental extension texts for the rental agency
withAI.pitchLine: "When a collision repair runs long, the rental customer gets a drafted extension message with the new date from the body shop."
withAI.whyItWorks: Rental extensions are constant during supplements. Both businesses save phone time.

withAI.route: Paint code helper for the supply house
withAI.pitchLine: "Shops type a color code and vehicle and get the supply house's matching mix notes and stock, without calling the counter."
withAI.whyItWorks: Counters lose hours to color questions. The shop client proves you know the workflow.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for accident calls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every missed call gets a text asking if the car is drivable, where it is and whether there's a claim number. The estimator calls back with the collision already sorted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the shop number forwarded and the wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Repair stage updates by text
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The owner gets a text at teardown, parts arrival, paint and reassembly, so the body shop stops fielding 'when's my car ready' calls."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the shop's repair stages and who marks each one.

softwareAI.name: Photo estimate intake with guided angles
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The driver is walked through the four corners and close-ups of the collision damage, so the estimator gets usable pictures the first time."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the estimator's must-have angles and where requests should go.

softwareAI.name: Damage triage from uploaded pictures
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Uploaded collision pictures are sorted into likely PDR, cosmetic panel or structural, so the estimator calls the big jobs first. A person still writes every estimate."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after the intake. Needs a few hundred past jobs with pictures and final repair type. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Rental and tow coordination board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every car in the body shop shows its rental status, tow-yard pickup and storage clock, so nobody pays avoidable storage fees."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their tow partners, rental partners and current tracking sheet.

softwareAI.name: Claim walkthrough chatbot for drivers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A driver asks 'do I have to use the insurer's shop' or 'what's a supplement' and gets the shop's own plain-language answer, with a reminder to check their policy."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the shop's claim walkthrough, reviewed by the owner. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Supplement documentation drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When teardown finds hidden damage, the tech's pictures and notes become a drafted supplement request for the estimator to check and send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs sample supplements and the shop's documentation habits. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Review responses written for collision customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Someone thanks the shop for a paint match on the quarter panel, and a reply mentioning that panel is drafted for the manager to send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Fleet damage portal by unit
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Fleet managers report van damage with pictures, approve collision estimates and see repair status per unit in one portal."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once a few fleets send work. Needs fleet unit lists and approval rules.

softwareAI.name: Paint booth and bay schedule
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which cars are in body, prep, the paint booth and reassembly, and spot the bottleneck before it costs a delivery date."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their stage list, booth count and a week of job flow.

softwareAI.name: Delivery-day walkthrough checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "At pickup the owner walks the car with a checklist: panel gaps, paint match, sensors and a clean interior, signed on a tablet."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the shop's quality-check list.

softwareAI.name: Calibration requirement lookup
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the vehicle and the panels being replaced, and see which sensors likely need recalibration, from the shop's own references, flagged for a tech to confirm."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the shop's calibration references and past jobs. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Hail event intake and scheduling
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a hailstorm hits, the hail page switches on, requests flow into assessment slots, and drivers get a time without calling."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Before hail season. Needs their assessment capacity per day.

softwareAI.name: Plain-language estimate explainer for owners
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each line of a collision estimate gets a short explanation an owner understands: blend, R&I, refinish hours and parts type."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs sample estimates and owner-approved wording. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Cycle time and comeback report
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See days-in-shop by repair type and which body jobs came back, so the owner fixes the slow stage instead of guessing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs job dates and comeback records for a few months.

softwareAI.name: Repair warranty registration for owners
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every repaired car's warranty is registered with the panels and paint done, and the owner or a later buyer can look it up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the shop's published warranty terms.

softwareAI.name: Parts arrival tracker with owner alerts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a back-ordered bumper or headlamp lands, the body shop's owner update goes out and the car moves back into a bay."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their parts ordering log.

softwareAI.name: Content writer for repair and town pages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A new collision repair or town page each month, drafted from finished jobs and approved by the owner before it goes live."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs monthly job notes and owner approval. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Customer repair history portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Owners can pull up every collision repair on their car, with before-and-after pictures, when they sell it or file another claim."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs the repair order archive.

softwareAI.name: Screener for body tech and painter applicants
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants answer questions on structural work, refinish experience and training before the manager spends time on an interview."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Guided damage pictures that land in the estimator's inbox ready to use. Every collision shop in the state wastes calls on blurry uploads."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first shop taught you the angles and routing. The product is ready to sell.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Shop finder for a paint and body supply distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Put a 'find a collision repair shop' map on your site for every body shop that buys your paint. Shops stay with the supplier who sends them cars."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors compete on loyalty. Sending shops work beats a rebate.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each body shop you acquire needs a claim walkthrough, photo intake and town pages under one brand. Template built, rollout per location."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Consolidators buy shops fast and need consistent sites.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every member collision shop gets the claim walkthrough, photo intake and choose-your-shop explainer as a member benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations look for tangible member perks. One deal reaches many shops.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label body shop template for automotive agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Automotive agencies sell body shops on marketing and still hand-build each site. License a collision template with the claim pages done."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the relationship; you sell them the part they rebuild every time.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Fleet damage management for regional fleets
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Regional delivery and service fleets report damage, approve estimates and track repairs across approved body shops in one portal."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Fleets pay annually to cut downtime, and the first shop client becomes the anchor repairer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Traveling PDR crews set up at partner body shops after each storm. A booking platform per event fills their days."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Storm chasers move constantly and pay per event. Body shops host the slots.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Consumer claim guide for a state consumer group
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A plain guide to collision repair claims and choosing a shop, for drivers across the state, built on the walkthrough we wrote for one shop."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Advocacy groups fund public guides. It positions the studio as the collision expert.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A calibration company serving dozens of body shops needs a booking site with a lookup by vehicle and panel."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Calibration is growing and sells only to shops. The collision client is the reference.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly sheet on which panels and lamps are back-ordered, built only from delays member shops report."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Parts delays drive cycle time. Contributed data keeps it honest and useful.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Collision template for a second metro's body shop
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A body shop in another metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one collision shop per market. You hold {City}; the shops two counties over still send drivers to a Facebook page."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography reuses the claim pages and before-and-after proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rebuild body shop sites lost with a marketing contract
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The body shop leaving an agency
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "When the marketing contract ended, the collision site went offline with it. I rebuild it on pages the shop owns outright."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Shops that lost a rented site already budgeted for one.

upsellLadder.offer: Body shop site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The collision site and the care plan go on one contract, so a hail banner or new estimator's number is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first collision repairs from site requests are delivered.
upsellLadder.line: "Those first site customers just got their cars back from the body shop. Every delivery should end with a review request."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention the counter drowning in status calls during supplements.
upsellLadder.line: "The status calls stop when the owner gets a text at teardown, paint and reassembly."

upsellLadder.trigger: A big structural collision job comes in, or the gallery has only a few before-and-afters.
upsellLadder.line: "That front-end collision in bay two is the shoot. Teardown to delivery becomes the body shop gallery for a year."

upsellLadder.offer: Photo estimate intake with guided angles
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of form data shows uploads too blurry or partial to estimate from.
upsellLadder.line: "Half the damage uploads miss the angle the estimator needs. Guided pictures fix that before the call."

upsellLadder.trigger: Hail season approaches, or a storm hits a nearby town.
upsellLadder.line: "The next hailstorm will flood the body shop's phones. Switch on the hail page and let the slots fill themselves."

upsellLadder.trigger: They complain about time spent writing supplements, or approvals stall cars.
upsellLadder.line: "Supplements are holding cars in the shop. Drafting them from the tech's pictures gets them out the door faster."

upsellLadder.trigger: A local fleet sends a third damaged van, or asks for invoicing by unit.
upsellLadder.line: "That fleet keeps sending vans. Give their manager a portal and the collision work stays with you."
